bionic: Keep dynamic property overrides out of loader ELF TLS

The staged PIF property change introduced a function-local thread_local
buffer in custom_rom_hide_get_prop_override(). This code is also linked
into the dynamic loader. The resulting alioth recovery linker64 contains
a PT_TLS segment, which soinfo::prelink_image() rejects with "TLS not
supported in loader" during loader startup. This can prevent both Android
and recovery from starting, before their UI appears.

Have each property API caller supply a PROP_VALUE_MAX stack buffer instead.
Preserve staged-property lookup, fixed overrides, the app-process guard,
and fallback to the real property when the staged value is empty. Separate
call-local storage also keeps nested callbacks from overwriting the outer
callback's dynamic property value.

Validation: inspected PT_TLS in the failing recovery linker64 and traced
the loader rejection in source; checked both callers, buffer lifetime and
git diff --check. A focused build was stopped at the user's request; no
completed rebuild or device boot verification is claimed. The fs_mgr
snapshot restoration is unchanged because no causal failure was established.

Fixes: 0fe98e0d800a ("custom_rom_hide: Mirror staged PIF product props")

custom_rom_hide: guard against invalid pointer args across all entry points

Some callers pass non-string sentinel values (e.g. 0x800000) instead of
a real pointer or null. The null check alone doesn't catch these, leading
to a SIGSEGV on dereference.

Add a low-address threshold check (< 0x10000) before any dereference in
all public and internal functions that take a path or property name.

custom_rom_hide: Keep substituting files opened with O_NOFOLLOW

"Harden custom ROM hiding and improve filesystem handling" made
can_filter_open() skip the substitution for O_NOFOLLOW, so an app
reading /proc/cmdline, /proc/filesystems, /proc/self/maps or mounts
with O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW got the unfiltered kernel contents back.

O_NOFOLLOW only concerns the last path component, and the substituted
paths are regular files. Filter them as before and hand the open back
to the kernel only when the last component is a symlink, such as
/proc/mounts, so the caller still gets ELOOP.

Signed-off-by: Quince <quinceroms@gmail.com>

custom_rom_hide: Preserve canonical proc paths for substituted files

The name recorded for a substituted file used the path exactly as
passed to open(). For proc files, readlink() on the descriptor then
returned aliases such as /proc/mounts, /proc/self/mounts or
/proc/thread-self/mounts instead of the kernel's canonical
/proc/<pid>/... and /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/... paths.

Resolve proc paths through an O_PATH descriptor before creating the
memfd name. Reuse the existing fd-link resolver so every proc
substitution uses the path selected by the kernel, independent of the
device or alias spelling. Keep non-proc paths and the existing fallback
unchanged.

fstat() and statx() on a substituted descriptor re-stat the recorded
canonical path. That path can name a task that no longer exists, for
example a file opened through /proc/thread-self by a thread that has
since exited, or a file belonging to another process that has gone. The
re-stat then fails and the memfd's own tmpfs device, mode and inode
showed through.

Capture the real file's stat and statx when the substitution is created,
while the canonical path still resolves, and keep the record alongside
the descriptor tracking bit. The re-stat of the canonical path stays the
primary source, so a live path still answers the caller's statx mask
exactly; the stored record is the fallback once that path is gone. The
record is carried across dup()/dup2() and freed when the descriptor is
closed or its number is substituted again. A lock guards the record's
lifetime so a concurrent fstat cannot read one that another thread is
freeing.

message:
core: spoof: Port TrickyStore, PIF and canary fetch fixes

Port TrickyStore reliability work on top of our EC/RSA issuer
fallback, empty-keybox reset, boot hash persistence, structural keybox
check and Evolver handling, and fix cases where PIF and TrickyStore
ended up unspoofed or inconsistent.

Keyboxes whose key algorithm does not match the certificate or private
key, whose private key does not sign for the first certificate, or
whose chain is not linked by issuer signatures are now rejected.
Validity dates are not enforced. Keybox-derived boot key and hash
fallbacks are re-derived when the keybox changes. The service keeps
the last good target, keybox and patch configuration when a fetch from
the activity manager fails, swaps in freshly parsed immutable
snapshots instead of clearing shared sets while attestations read
them, and fingerprints keybox payloads with SHA-256.

Attestation reuses the boot key and hash the TEE measured in the
original leaf instead of rebuilding them, keeping the original layout
for older Keymaster RootOfTrust. It no longer re-signs leaves already
signed by the active keybox, verifies new leaves against the issuer
and bails out on malformed KeyDescription data. The TEE boot hash
probe is hardened and removes its probe key afterwards. In Keystore
the hack or generate decision is made per request using the process
UID, probe aliases and ordinary keys are left alone, non-attested
certificates skip a second Keystore read, and a failed hardware
attestation falls back to a software keybox-signed key.

PIF now retries loading its config lazily, rate limited and only after
boot in system_server, so a process that started before ActivityManager
or Settings were ready is not left unspoofed for its whole lifetime. A
missing SECURITY_PATCH is derived from the build ID, and
DEVICE_INITIAL_SDK_INT comes from a per-device table in
PixelDeviceRepository that AxSpoofManager's auto-refresh shares, so
first_api_level matches the spoofed device instead of always claiming
the Pixel 6a's.

Canary device discovery in PixelDeviceRepository accepts factory image
and OTA pages for either a QPR or the base release and takes the
newest, so early in a release cycle, when only the base release has
beta pages, it no longer falls back to an older version. The Flash
Tool API key is read from the page's data-client-config attribute
first and only then from a scan of the whole page.

core: Fix spoofing structure

existing design was based on module structure and legacy prop hook spoofing. that design only works with hardcoded spoof values and code injection like lsposed or magisk. for proper aosp integration it falls apart, /data/adb exposes root detection signals and leaks identity to apps because the spoof logic runs under the calling process context instead of system_server.

old flow
process -> spoof runs inside process, uses process identity -> hits selinux denials and content provider denials if we tried to route through settings provider

new flow
process -> am binder -> am -> spoof runs in system_server -> no denials, no identity leak

core: pif: Keep the numeric release when the fingerprint says CANARY

A Canary fingerprint carries the literal CANARY where the Android
release goes, so deriving RELEASE from it spoofed Build.VERSION.RELEASE

description.

release in deriveFieldsFromFingerprint() rather than expanding the

vendor partitions only, and ro.build.description, ro.build.flavor and the

Derive type, tags, description (product-type release id incremental tags)
and flavor from the fingerprint, honoring explicit TYPE/TAGS/RELEASE/ID/
INCREMENTAL/PRODUCT and *.build.type/*.build.tags config entries, and stage
them for bionic. AlwaysStrong's prop_unify does the same system-wide with

spoof: Rework PIF and TrickyStore, add native refresh

Make the PIF and TrickyStore attestation output consistent with
itself and with real KeyMint, and keep it current without the

  getCertificateChain() throws when it is set, so it never bypasses
  the keybox attestation.
- Make spoofVendingSdk a level (1 = SDK 32, never above the real SDK)
  applied to Play Store instead of DroidGuard.

  RELEASE from FINGERPRINT when the config omits them.

  overrides, including custom exact and wildcard entries, for bionic.

- Emit attestation AuthorizationLists in ascending tag order with the
  padding, EC curve, RSA exponent and MGF1 digests actually requested,
  and derive KeyUsage from the key purposes.
- Take the boot key from ro.boot.vbmeta.public_key_digest, the keybox
  or a persisted value, and persist the boot hash.
- Replace the attestation IDs of a hacked chain with the PIF profile
  and pass the calling packages so per-package patch levels apply.

  advisory and keep the loaded keyboxes when a document is truncated
  or holds no key, instead of clearing them.
- Add a SKIP target mode, a shared Xposed manager exclusion and a
  default target list. Support YYYY-MM-DD patch templates, re-check a
  broken TEE after five minutes and cache revoked serials for seven
  days when the revocation fetch fails.

  with the highest build id, stop on a bot wall and derive the patch
  date from the build id. Prefer A-series devices in the picker.

sepolicy: Label the Play Integrity staging props

The persist.sys.pif.* props that AxSpoofManager stages for bionic fell
under the persist.sys. prefix, which is system_prop and readable by
every domain. bionic hides them from app processes other than DroidGuard,
but that only covers reads that go through libc, so anything that maps
the property area directly could still see the staged identity.

Give them their own type. pif_prop is a system internal property,
written by system_server, which stages the values and reads them back
to skip rewrites, and read by gmscore_app, the domain DroidGuard runs
in. gmscore_app is a coredomain, so the system_internal_prop neverallow
for other domains is not affected. Every other domain, including
regular apps, loses read access to the props.

The prefix entry has no exact match, so it covers all the staging props
under persist.sys.pif. and takes precedence over the persist.sys.
prefix. Debug builds get read access for shell so the staged values can
be checked with getprop; user builds do not.

+data class BouncerPromptMessage(

+@Composable
+fun BouncerPrompt(
+    title: String,
+    subtitle: String? = null,
+    isError: Boolean = false,
+    modifier: Modifier = Modifier
+) {
+    val message = remember(title, subtitle, isError) {
+        BouncerPromptMessage(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, isError = isError)
+    }
+
+    Crossfade(
+        targetState = message,
+        label = "BouncerPromptCrossfade",
+        animationSpec = tween(durationMillis = 200, easing = FastOutSlowInEasing),
+        modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth()
+    ) { currentMessage ->
+        PromptContent(currentMessage)
+    }
+}
+
+@Composable
+private fun PromptContent(message: BouncerPromptMessage) {
+    val titleColor = if (message.isError) {
+        MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error
+    } else {
+        MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface
+    }
+    val subtitleColor = if (message.isError) {
+        MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error
+    } else {
+        MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
+    }
+
+    Column(

+        modifier = Modifier
+            .fillMaxWidth()
+            .padding(horizontal = 16.dp)
+    ) {
+        Text(

+            style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineMedium,
+            color = titleColor,
+            textAlign = TextAlign.Center,
+            overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
+            maxLines = 1
+        )
+
+        message.subtitle?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }?.let {

+        }
+    }

+private fun createMorphingPath(
